root_cause: The direct-recursion self-inlining check was changed from reading the builder's own always-valid MaglevCompilationUnit pointer to instead reading MaglevGraphLabeller-derived provenance data, which is only guaranteed to be populated when GDB JIT interface support or graph tracing is active. This coupled a functional correctness check to an optional, debug-only subsystem, producing a null-pointer dereference when that subsystem was disabled (the common release-build case).
findings: When MaglevGraphBuilder::CanInlineCall was moved/refactored into the shared MaglevReducer<BaseT>::CanInlineCall template, the direct-recursion self-inlining guard was rewritten from comparing against the builder's own `compilation_unit_->shared_function_info()` to instead reading `current_provenance().unit->shared_function_info()`. `current_provenance()` returns the MaglevGraphLabeller::Provenance
